headline: AI Agent built to book doctor appointments and archive lab reports using GPT-4o vision
summary: A new tutorial details building an AI agent with GPT-4o and Browser-use to automate tedious healthcare tasks like booking appointments and managing lab reports, bypassing traditional automation's limitations.
details: Frustrated by clunky hospital web portals for booking check-ups or downloading lab results? A new tutorial demonstrates how to build an AI agent that can automate these tedious healthcare administration tasks.

The agent leverages GPT-4o and the Browser-use library with Playwright to navigate complex user interfaces. Unlike traditional automation tools that rely on brittle DOM selectors, this agent "sees" the page like a human, understanding visual cues.

The system operates on a feedback loop: the LLM perceives the browser state via screenshots and DOM trees, decides on an action, and executes it using Playwright. This allows it to handle dynamic web elements and updates.

The agent can manage complex authentication, including notifying users for captchas or solving simple ones with vision-to-text. It can also route downloaded files, like lab reports, to specific directories for further processing.

Once reports are downloaded, they can be processed into a vector database, enabling users to query their health data. This transforms static PDFs into actionable information, allowing for trend analysis.
While prototyping is straightforward, building a production-ready agent requires robust architecture to handle edge cases such as session timeouts, dynamic pop-ups, and multi-factor authentication.

This development signifies a shift towards software adapting to users, rather than the other way around. By combining GPT-4o's vision with Browser-use, AI gains the ability to interact with web interfaces intelligently.
